# Independent correctness review: Sol Max MARC21 Rust

Run UID: `6f26394a-2304-4335-813c-5d5902d70c0e`  
Task/model: `marc21-rs`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, Max  
Eval: MARC21 `3.0.2`; Codex CLI `0.153.4`  
Review date: October 1, 2026 (Chicago; artifacts timestamped October 2 UTC)

## Disposition

Approve the recorded **2,900/2,900 (100%)** result for publication, subject to
the parent's separate accounting/network/provenance checks. There is no
correctness-review reason to exclude or regenerate this run. This is a
completed benchmark result, not a claim of exhaustive MARC/XML conformance.

Both `result.json` and `test-report.json` contain 2,900 passed cases, with no
failed, errored, skipped, or duplicated node IDs. Their node-ID sets match.
Build succeeded, grading completed, and both generation exit fields say
`completed`. Accordingly there are **no failed-case defect groups** to explain
and no nonzero timeout or interrupted-work score to qualify.

## Evidence reviewed

Reviewed the canonical transcript's beginning-to-end command/message/event
sequence, substantive command outputs (including document-derived rule tables,
builds and self-tests), final source modules and embedded field table, result
metadata, every report outcome, and the frozen request/base prompt and MARCXML
structural reference. Relevant LOC corpus excerpts in the transcript cover
leader/directory structure, fixed fields, repeatability, local tags, embedded
holdings and special 880/886 handling. No submitted code was executed on the
host; this was static review of the preserved artifacts and existing grading.

## Implementation and completion assessment

This is a substantive, self-contained standard-library Rust implementation,
not a wrapper around an external MARC utility. Cargo's dependency table is
empty. JSON/base64 parsing, request/error handling, ISO 2709 byte layout,
MARCXML parsing/rendering, and shared bibliographic validation are implemented
in source; the field rules are embedded using `include_str!` and do not require
the mounted documentation at runtime.

The implementation checks the leader, directory lengths/offsets/coverage and
terminators, decodes field text with Rust's checked UTF-8 conversion, preserves
physical field order separately from sorted directory order, and computes
serialization lengths from bytes. Shared validation uses an extracted field
table for indicator values, subfield membership and repeatability, plus
explicit fixed-field and special-field logic. The XML layer checks namespace,
root/collection cardinality, child ordering, required attributes and normalized
leader output. These mechanisms agree with the tested public contract and
make the full score credible.

The transcript shows iterative work and voluntary completion. It ends after
successful Cargo unit tests (five tests), a release build, Unicode four-action
round trips and malformed-input/repeatability rejection checks. The agent then
used `cargo clean` to remove generated build artifacts, retained all source,
and explicitly delivered the finished implementation. There is no request for
clarification/continuation, quota stop, timeout, or unfinished work at exit.

Minor tooling issues were nonblocking: `cargo fmt` was unavailable, the optional
`file` utility was missing, one local documentation extraction script failed
before being corrected, and an `rg` query had no matches. Subsequent builds and
tests succeeded. None warrants excluding the run or rerunning generation.

## Claims and contamination

The final message claims all four actions, Unicode ISO 2709, namespaces and
collections, leader normalization, field validation and structured errors, and
lists successful tests. Those claims are supported at the measured benchmark
scope. It does not claim to have run or seen the hidden 2,900-case suite.

The command sequence uses local mounted documentation, local source edits,
Cargo without external dependencies, and agent-written Python test drivers.
No GitHub fetch/clone, HTTP client download, browser/search invocation, package
installation, hidden-test access, or reference-solution access appears in the
canonical event stream. URLs in document output and XML namespace literals
are not evidence of fetching them. Detailed proxy/session audit and source
manifest identity remain the parent's separate responsibility. Preserve the
local-versus-source Docker image distinction in publication notes.

## Scope caveat from static inspection

Full benchmark success is not proof that the hand-written XML parser implements
every XML lexical rule. In `xml.rs`, the start-tag attribute loop calls
`whitespace()` without requiring any whitespace to have been consumed between
successive attributes (around line 177), so adjacent quoted attributes such as
`tag="245"ind1="1"` appear capable of being accepted. `name_token` (line 143)
also permits only ASCII name characters, potentially rejecting valid
non-ASCII namespace prefixes. These are static-review observations outside the
recorded failed-case set; they were not reproduced by executing the submission
and do not change the frozen 2,900/2,900 score. No tests, prompts, submission
files, or scoring were changed.

Suggested Last Message summary: Claims complete; delivered a self-contained
Rust implementation of all four MARC actions and reported successful build,
Unicode round-trip and rejection tests. All 2,900 hidden checks passed.
